newsitem.title: UK: SFA rejects GFEC spot-rolling forex application.
newsitem.headline: SFA rejects GFEC spot-rolling forex application.

text.p: The Securities and Futures Authority said on Friday it has denied authorisation to Global Foreign Exchange Corporation Ltd (GFEC) to provide speculative foreign exchange services know as rolling-spot forex contracts.

"After a thorough evaluation of GFEC's application...SFA, through its Authorisation Committee, has today determined that GFEC does not meet the standards of fitness and propriety required for authorisation," the SFA said in a release.
GFEC, which applied for authorisation to deal in rolling-spot forex contracts on February 29 1996, became on Friday the first firm to be denied such authorisation, said the SFA.

A rolling-spot forex contract, a seven-day agreement to buy or sell foreign currency, falls under the jurisdiction of the Securities and Investment Board (SIB) because as a forward contract it constitutes an investment.
The SFA said GFEC has 20 business days to appeal against their decision before an SFA Authorisation Appeal Tribunal.
Aside from GFEC, the SFA said it has also received authorisation applications from 29 rolling-spot forex firms; thirteen of which have subsequently withdrawn their application.
Ten firms have been granted authorisation and six applications are still being considered, said the SFA.

While the GFEC is the first company to be denied such approval, the SFA said it is now up to the SIB to decided on interim permission for it to continue in rolling spot forex operations while it considers an appeal against the SFA.
